title: DuckDB function ST_AsMVT — ST_AsMVT
text: Make Mapbox Vector Tile set geometries properties function takes input row type (STRUCT) containing geometry column number property columns. returns single binary BLOB containing Mapbox Vector Tile. function following signature: ST_AsMVT(row STRUCT, layer_name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'layer', extent INTEGER DEFAULT 4096, geom_column_name VARCHAR DEFAULT NULL, feature_id_column_name VARCHAR DEFAULT NULL) -> BLOB first argument struct containing geometry properties. second argument name layer vector tile. argument optional defaults 'layer'. third argument extent tile. argument optional defaults 4096. fourth argument name geometry column input row. argument optional. provided, first geometry column input row used. multiple geometry columns present, error raised. fifth argument name feature id column input row. argument optional. provided, values column used feature ids vector tile. column must type INTEGER BIGINT. set negative NULL, feature id assigned corresponding feature. input struct must contain exactly one geometry column type GEOMETRY. can contain number property columns types VARCHAR, FLOAT, DOUBLE, INTEGER, BIGINT, BOOLEAN. Example:   example creates vector tile named 'cities' extent 4096 'cities' table, using 'geom' geometry column 'id' feature id column. However, probably want use ST_AsMVTGeom function first transform clip geometries tile extent. following example assumes geometry WebMercator ("EPSG:3857") coordinates. Replace {z}, {x}, {y} appropriate tile coordinates, {table} table name, {tile_path} path write tile .
code: SELECT ST_AsMVT({'geom': geom, 'id': id, 'name': name}, 'cities', 4096, 'geom', 'id') AS tile FROM cities; COPY (     SELECT ST_AsMVT({{         "geometry": ST_AsMVTGeom(             geometry,             ST_Extent(ST_TileEnvelope({z}, {x}, {y})),             4096,             256,             false         )     }})     FROM {your table} WHERE ST_Intersects(geometry, ST_TileEnvelope({z}, {x}, {y})) ) to {tile_path} (FORMAT 'BLOB'); ```.
